bib.title: Chain-of-Table: Evolving Tables in the Reasoning Chain for Table Understanding

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Chain-of-Table: Evolving Tables in the Reasoning Chain for Table Understanding. Zilong Wang, Hao Zhang, Chun-Liang Li, Julian Martin Eisenschlos, Vincent Perot, Zifeng Wang, Lesly Miculicich, Yasuhisa Fujii, Jingbo Shang, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister (UCSD, Google Cloud AI Research, Google Research). Venue: ICLR 2024 (the header reads "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024"). arXiv:2401.04398v2, 19 Jan 2024.

COVERAGE: 24 of 24 pages. Extraction was clean. I read about 66,000 of 80,997 chars in full: main text, all tables, Appendices A to F, and the start and end of the prompt figures. I skimmed the middle of the appendix prompt-figure listings (Figs 9-18, about 66k to 78k chars) and only checked their structure. The reference list was skimmed.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Chain-of-Table beats every generic and program-aided baseline on WikiTQ and TabFact with all three backbones.
  number: PaLM 2 TabFact 86.61 vs best baseline Dater 84.63 (+1.98); WikiTQ 67.31 vs Dater 61.48 (+5.83). GPT-3.5 TabFact 80.20 (+1.03); WikiTQ 59.94 (+3.20). LLaMA 2 TabFact 67.24 (+2.12); WikiTQ 42.61 (+1.17).
  setup: Table 1. Backbones are PaLM 2-S, GPT 3.5 (turbo-16k-0613) and LLaMA 2 (Llama-2-17B-chat; the extraction prints "17B", sic). Few-shot demos come from the training set. WikiTQ is scored by denotation accuracy and TabFact by binary accuracy. Baselines are End-to-End QA, Few-Shot QA, CoT, Text-to-SQL, Binder and Dater.
  quote: "CHAIN -OF-TABLE (ours) 86.61 (+1.98) 67.31 (+5.83) 80.20 (+1.03) 59.94 (+3.20) 67.24 (+2.12) 42.61 (+1.17)"
  where: p.6, Table 1

- Vanilla CoT gives little or negative gain on tables. Baseline rows from Table 1, in the order PaLM2 TabFact, PaLM2 WikiTQ, GPT-3.5 TabFact, GPT-3.5 WikiTQ, LLaMA2 TabFact, LLaMA2 WikiTQ:
  number: End-to-End QA 77.92, 60.59, 70.45, 51.84, 44.86, 23.90. Few-Shot QA 78.06, 60.33, 71.54, 52.56, 62.01, 35.52. CoT 79.05, 60.43, 65.37, 53.48, 60.52, 36.05. So CoT falls below End-to-End on PaLM 2 WikiTQ (60.43 vs 60.59), and on GPT-3.5 TabFact it drops to 65.37 from Few-Shot's 71.54.
  setup: As in the first claim.
  quote: "Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al., 2022) 79.05 60.43 65.37 53.48 60.52 36.05" and "we observe a performance decrease on WikiTQ due to the complexity of tabular structure when vanilla Chain-of-Thought is introduced to End-to-End QA using PaLM 2."
  where: p.6-7

- Gain over End-to-End QA with PaLM 2.
  number: 8.69% on TabFact and 6.72% on WikiTQ.
  setup: PaLM 2. The paper does not say whether these are absolute points. 86.61-77.92 = 8.69, so they are absolute points.
  quote: "our proposed C HAIN -OF-TABLE consistently enhances End-to-End QA performance by 8.69% on TabFact and 6.72% on WikiTQ with PaLM 2."
  where: p.7

- Program-aided baselines are unstable across model sizes. Binder is strong on larger models but weaker on small LLaMA 2.
  number: Binder GPT-3.5 TabFact 79.17 and WikiTQ 56.74, against LLaMA 2 WikiTQ 30.92. Text-to-SQL PaLM 2 TabFact 68.37 is below End-to-End's 77.92.
  setup: Table 1. The authors attribute this to single-pass generation over a static table.
  quote: "Binder, perform better on larger LLMs but its performance decreases with smaller LLaMA 2 (Llama-2-17B-chat). We attribute this decline to Binder's single-pass generation process."
  where: p.7

- Larger gain on long tables.
  number: Small (<2k tokens): Binder 56.54, Dater 62.50, CoT-table 68.13 (+5.63). Medium (2k-4k): 26.13 / 42.34 / 52.25 (+9.91). Large (>4k): 6.41 / 34.62 / 44.87 (+10.25).
  setup: Table 3, WikiTQ, PaLM 2 presumed (the text does not state the model for Table 3). Bins are by token count.
  quote: "CHAIN -OF-TABLE (ours) 68.13 (+5.63) 52.25 (+9.91) 44.87 (+10.25)"
  where: p.8, Table 3

- Fewer LLM samples per question than Binder or Dater, because it uses greedy search rather than self-consistency.
  number: Binder 50 samples, Dater 100, Chain-of-Table at most 25 (DynamicPlan up to 5, GenerateArgs up to 19, Query 1). The paper says 50% less than Binder and 75% less than Dater.
  setup: WikiTQ, Table 4. This counts generated samples and is not a latency or cost measure. Chain-of-Table still makes iterative calls.
  quote: "the number of queries needed by CHAIN -OF-TABLE is the lowest among the most recent baselines – 50% less than Binder and 75% less than Dater."
  where: p.9

- Accuracy declines as the required operation chain gets longer, but Chain-of-Table declines more gently.
  number: WikiTQ chain lengths 1 to 5, Chain-of-Table 51.6 / 73.0 / 69.5 / 61.0 / 60.1 (read from the Fig. 3 extraction; the mapping to series is garbled). The margin is up to 11.6 points over CoT and up to 7.9 over Dater. Sample counts by chain length, WikiTQ: 95, 1308, 1481, 1084, 341. TabFact: 4, 547, 732, 517, 223.
  setup: PaLM 2, WikiTQ, Fig. 3 and Table 2. Most samples need 2 to 4 operations. Only samples that require operations are analysed.
  quote: "with a significant margin up to 11.6% compared with Chain-of-Table" is NOT the printed text. The printed text is: "consistently surpasses both baseline methods across all operation chain lengths, with a significant margin up to 11.6% compared with Chain-of-Thought, and up to 7.9% compared with Dater."
  where: p.7-8

- Ablation: removing any one of the five operations lowers accuracy.
  number: Full model TabFact 86.61, WikiTQ 67.31. Without f_add_column: 85.23 (-1.38) / 65.88 (-1.43). Without f_select_column: 82.61 (-4.00) / 65.68 (-1.63). Without f_select_row: 82.21 (-4.40) / 65.06 (-2.25). Without f_group_by: 84.78 (-1.83) / 61.88 (-5.43). Without f_sort_by: 86.21 (-0.40) / 65.85 (-1.46).
  setup: PaLM 2, Table 5, leave-one-out. Row and column selection matter most on TabFact. Group-by matters most on WikiTQ.
  quote: "w/o f_group_by() 84.78 (-1.83) 61.88 (-5.43)"
  where: p.13, Table 5

- FeTaQA (free-form QA) improves slightly, but the authors say ROUGE under-rewards correct answers.
  number: BLEU 32.61 vs Dater 29.47 (+3.14); ROUGE-1 0.66 vs 0.63; ROUGE-2 0.44 vs 0.41; ROUGE-L 0.56 vs 0.53. End-to-End QA BLEU is 28.37.
  setup: PaLM 2, Table 6. Dater matches End-to-End on all three ROUGE scores (0.63 / 0.41 / 0.53).
  quote: "CHAIN -OF-TABLE (ours) 32.61 (+3.14) 0.66 (+0.03) 0.44 (+0.03) 0.56 (+0.03)"
  where: p.14

- Table serialisation format changes accuracy. PIPE is best, and the others are 2 to 4.5 points lower.
  number: End-to-End QA, WikiTQ, PaLM 2: PIPE 60.6, HTML 56.1, TSV 58.1, Markdown 58.0.
  setup: Table 10. This is End-to-End QA only, not the Chain-of-Table method.
  quote: "End-to-End QA 60.6 56.1 58.1 58.0"
  where: p.16, App. D

- Method is in-context only, with a small demo budget.
  number: 29 annotated demo samples overall, shared across datasets. Temperature 0.0 for planning, group_by, sort_by and query. Temperature 1.0 (WikiTQ, FeTaQA) or 0.5 (TabFact) with 8 samples for select_row and select_column.
  setup: App. C, Tables 7-9. Demos come from the training set.
  quote: "Overall, we annotate 29 samples and use them across different datasets."
  where: p.15

METHOD (for the note)
- Loop: the LLM picks the next operation from a pool of five (f_add_column, f_select_row, f_select_column, f_group_by, f_sort_by), then generates its arguments. The operation is executed programmatically on the table, and the new table is fed back. This repeats until the [E] tag. The final table and the question go to the LLM to answer. The reasoning is carried in the evolving table, not in text.
- App. E.1: the DynamicPlan prompt asks the LLM to complete the whole remaining chain, but only the first operation is kept. Later operations are not based on the up-to-date table, so they may be wrong.
- Arguments are parsed with regular expressions.
- Tables are serialised in PIPE format ("col : ... / row 1 : ... | ...").

LIMITS
- Only five operations are used. The authors say more can be added, "which we leave for future work".
- Only three table benchmarks (WikiTQ, TabFact, FeTaQA) and three mid-size 2023 models: PaLM 2-S, GPT-3.5-turbo-16k-0613 and Llama-2 chat. No frontier or reasoning models. This has dated: current models handle tables natively and the numbers are not comparable.
- Gains on GPT-3.5 and LLaMA 2 are small (+1.0 to +3.2, and +1.17 on LLaMA 2 WikiTQ). The largest gains are on PaLM 2.
- The Dater-with-Codex result (65.9% WikiTQ, 85.6% TabFact) is excluded because Codex is gone. In a footnote on p.6, Dater with Codex scores higher than Chain-of-Table's GPT-3.5 and LLaMA 2 results on WikiTQ and TabFact, and higher on WikiTQ than Chain-of-Table's PaLM 2 result of 67.31 (65.9 is lower; the TabFact 85.6 is below 86.61). The SOTA claim therefore depends on that exclusion.
- Baselines were re-run by the authors with Codex swapped for the new backbones.
- FeTaQA ROUGE gains are marginal, and the authors admit the metric is insensitive.
- The efficiency analysis counts samples only. There are no latency, token or cost figures, and the loop is multi-call.
- Table 3's model is not stated, and there is no error analysis.

BUILDS ON: Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al., 2022); Least-to-Most (Zhou et al., 2022); Decomposed Prompting (Khot et al., 2022); Program-of-Thought (Chen et al., 2022); PAL (Gao et al., 2023); Tree-of-Thought (Yao et al., 2023); Binder (Cheng et al., 2022); Dater (Ye et al., 2023); Text-to-SQL with LLMs (Rajkumar et al., 2022); "Large language models are few(1)-shot table reasoners" (Chen, 2023, source of CoT demos); LEVER (Ni et al., 2023); Tab-CoT (Jin & Lu, 2023); TAPEX (Liu et al., 2021). Benchmarks: WikiTQ (Pasupat & Liang, 2015), TabFact (Chen et al., 2019), FeTaQA (Nan et al., 2022).

CODE (verbatim, p.18, Fig. 9 prompt style)
- "Function Chain: f_add_column(Country) ->"
- Completion: "f_select_row(row 1, row 10) -> f_select_column(Country) -> f_group_by(Country) -> <END>"
- Algorithm 1 (p.4): "repeat / f ← DynamicPlan(T,Q,chain) / args ← GenerateArgs(T,Q,f) / T ← f(T,args) / chain ← chain.append((f,args)) / until f = [E] / Â ← Query(T, Q)"

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): generic reasoning vs program-aided reasoning vs Chain-of-Table on the cyclist-country question. It shows why a static table fails (the "Country" is inside the "Cyclist" cell, so SQL cannot parse it) and the add_col, select_row, group_by, sort_by chain.
- Fig 2 (p.5): DynamicPlan and GenerateArgs inputs.
- Fig 3 (p.7): accuracy by operation chain length (CoT vs Dater vs Chain-of-Table).
- Fig 4 (p.9): worked example of the NAACP awards question with intermediate tables.
- Fig 6 (p.17): DynamicPlan prompt template (atomic-op demo, chain demo, input).
- Fig 9 (p.18): the actual WikiTQ prompt.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Figure 3 numbers are scrambled in the extraction, so the mapping of values to series is uncertain and I used the text's "up to 11.6 / 7.9" instead. I did not verify the Fig. 3 per-length values. The middle prompt-figure pages (Figs 10-17) were only skimmed. I did not run the figures.py caption script. The footnote comparison on Dater+Codex is my reading of the printed numbers and is not stated by the authors in that form. Please check the claim in the LIMITS entry about "higher on WikiTQ than PaLM 2": 65.9 < 67.31, so Codex-Dater is NOT higher than Chain-of-Table PaLM 2 on either dataset. It is higher than the GPT-3.5 (59.94 WikiTQ, 80.20 TabFact) and LLaMA 2 results only because those are different backbones. Treat the SOTA caveat as: the comparison against Codex-Dater was not run.
